verdicts.claim: A checkpoint transfers committed transactions from the WAL file back into the original database file. It must sync the WAL befo
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage ... database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL."

verdicts.claim: Automatic checkpointing is on by default with a 1000-page threshold ... PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint ... 0 or negative disables
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "Setting the auto-checkpoint size to zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off ... All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE ... enabled by default with an interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT."

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE never invokes the busy handler. FULL waits until no active writer and every reader on latest snapshot; blocks new writers
verdicts.evidence: checkpoint_v2: FULL "blocks new database writers while it is pending"; TRUNCATE "truncates the log file to zero bytes"; NOOP "always checkpoints zero frames".

verdicts.claim: journal_size_limit (default -1, unlimited) applied at commit or WAL reset shrinks it; last connection close deletes -wal unless PERSIST_WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "Each time a transaction is committed or a WAL file resets ... truncated to the limit ... default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)"; wal.html names SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL retention.

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs PASSIVE at 1000 pages (MinCheckpointPageN) and every 1 minute; above 121,359 pages (~500 MB) passive-first, added v0.5.15
Setting truncate-page-n to 0 disables the blocking step for apps with long-lived readers, which then must monitor WAL size
verdicts.evidence: Litestream: "Applications with long-lived read transactions: Set truncate-page-n: 0"; "If you disable TruncatePageN, you must implement: Disk space monitoring".

verdicts.claim: With synchronous=NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation that issues a sync; run checkpoints from separate thread/process
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation".

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint starvation: overlapping readers can prevent completion indefinitely, and the WAL grows without bound
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: "if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound."

verdicts.claim: If busy handler returns 0 during FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE wait, checkpoints like PASSIVE and returns SQLITE_BUSY; checkpoint lock held -> BUSY
verdicts.evidence: checkpoint_v2: "If the busy-handler returns 0 ... proceeds ... in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE ... SQLITE_BUSY is returned"; "Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case."

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row (busy, log frames, checkpointed frames); busy=1 if blocked; frame columns -1 if no WAL
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: "returns a single row with three integer columns ... 1 if a RESTART or FULL or TRUNCATE checkpoint was blocked ... second and third column are -1 if there is no" WAL.
